intro: An exposed pedal solo opens a work that moves between free figuration, a fugue and a quick chaconne. Its contrasting forms are connected by related musical material rather than separated into independent movements.
question: Can you recognise how the opening pedal gesture changes when other voices take it up?

sections.label: Ciacona · approximate
sections.mNote: a three-bar bass ground supports the final variation span

cues.title: The feet begin alone
cues.text: The opening line belongs to the organ pedals, with the manuals resting. A single low-register gesture therefore introduces both the instrument’s independent bass and material that will matter later in the fugue.
cues.evidence: The score opens with a pedal solo. Relf Clark relates the later fugue subject to the opening pedal figure: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201.

cues.title: An organ can change its texture
cues.text: Follow the difference between a single running line and several notes sounding together. In this prelude, chords, passagework and rests change the density even though every sound comes from the same instrument.
cues.evidence: The opening 35 bars alternate free textures; the report has a change near 0:34 and a relatively quieter span around 0:35–0:55. This is a listening prompt, not an identification of the organist’s stops: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: An organist in Lübeck
cues.text: Buxtehude became organist of Lübeck’s Marienkirche in 1668. He also developed its public Abendmusiken, a concert tradition inherited from his predecessor Franz Tunder. His duties extended beyond playing for services.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s historical account documents the appointment and Abendmusiken: https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude.

cues.title: One subject, successive voices
cues.text: The quieter fugal span asks you to track a recurring subject as it passes between voices. Unlike the opening’s freer gestures, its continuity comes from recognisable material entering against lines already in motion.
cues.evidence: The score’s fugue begins at bar 36 after the prelude. The report has a strong change at 1:48 and a pronounced level drop around 1:45–1:55; the placement is approximate, not an aligned first-note claim: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Keep one line in attention
cues.text: Choose a voice for a few seconds, then listen for another line against it. The organ can sustain several lines without their articulations coinciding; the subject’s return does not erase what the other voices are doing.
cues.evidence: The fugue’s independent entries and continuing counterpoint are visible in score bars 36–64. This prompt does not assign a particular entry to this timestamp: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Bach’s long absence
cues.text: In 1705 the young Bach travelled to Lübeck to hear Buxtehude. The Arnstadt authorities later questioned why his leave had lasted much longer than granted. That documented visit shows Buxtehude’s attraction to another working organist; it does not prove Bach heard this particular prelude.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s account cites Bach’s obituary and the Arnstadt consistory record of 21 February 1706: https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude.

cues.title: The fugue releases its pattern
cues.text: The later free continuation moves away from regular subject entries into runs, chords and held bass notes. Listen for the contrast between quick surface movement and a lower note that can remain fixed beneath it.
cues.evidence: The score’s bars 65–74 loosen the fugal texture before the Ciacona. The report marks changes at 3:06, 3:10, 3:28 and 3:38, with a strong level increase around 3:28. This broad span is not labelled as a precisely aligned bar: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A short ground, changing upper parts
cues.text: The Presto Ciacona uses a three-bar bass pattern for eight statements. Above it, the writing changes: listen for how a recurring foundation can support different densities and shapes rather than a literal repeat of the whole texture.
cues.evidence: Relf Clark identifies eight statements of a three-bar ground; the score marks Ciacona at bar 75 in 3/2. A feature change at 3:48, after the sustained dominant region, supports the approximate start of this final span: https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201; https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A modern instrument in Gerstetten
cues.text: Fabian Wöhrle plays the Reiser organ built in 1984 for the Catholic church of St Peter and St Paul in Gerstetten. This is not Buxtehude’s own instrument. The recording lets the historical music speak through a different organ and room.
cues.evidence: The Commons description identifies performer, church and the Reiser organ, II/P/22, 1984: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:D._Buxtehude_Pr%C3%A4ludium%2C_Fuge_und_Chaconne_C-Dur_BuxWV_137_Fabian_W%C3%B6hrle_Kath._Kirche_Gerstetten.mp3.

cues.title: The room after the final chord
cues.text: The closing harmony is held, then its sound decays into the room. The resonance continues after the last active movement of the musical lines; give it time before starting another recording.
cues.evidence: The report shows no detected onsets in the 4:50 and 4:55 windows, while relative level drops from −4.4 dB to −34.8 dB and then to the noise floor by 5:00. This describes the release region, not an exact key-release instant.

transitions.title: Free gestures give way to imitation
transitions.how: After the opening’s varied chordal and running textures, one line presents a subject for other voices to take up. The subject is related to the early pedal gesture, so the fugue establishes a new procedure without discarding the opening material.
transitions.evidence: The score begins its fugal writing at bar 36; Clark describes the relation to the opening pedal figure. The report marks 1:48 and the following quiet region: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201.

transitions.title: The last entry opens into freer writing
transitions.how: The final subject entry leads on without a separate movement break. Its counterpoint loosens into quicker runs and chordal gestures, allowing the organist’s bass to alternate motion with sustained support. The connection is continuous rather than a new fugue subject.
transitions.evidence: Clark identifies the final entry at bar 64 and its unbroken continuation into free writing. Score bars 65–74 show the changing textures. The report changes at 3:06 and 3:10 place this join approximately: https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201; https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.

transitions.title: A triple-time ground fixes the next pattern
transitions.how: The free continuation reaches its sustained close, then the Ciacona establishes a three-bar bass ground in triple metre. The bass now returns by design, while the upper parts vary around it. This replaces the free span’s flexible gestures with a recurring framework.
transitions.evidence: The inspected score changes from common time to 3/2 and marks Presto Ciacona at bar 75. The report’s 3:48 change follows the long dominant around 3:42–3:47; the boundary is passage-level: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf.
